recognize_zh: 臨床照片中下肢皮膚可見多發暗紫紅色、表面光亮的隆起腫瘤結節，周圍伴隨較平坦的紅斑與浸潤性斑塊（patch/plaque），同時存在不同階段病灶，符合蕈狀肉芽腫腫瘤期（tumor stage mycosis fungoides）。
features: Clinical photograph of the lower limb with multiple violaceous, dome-shaped, shiny tumor nodules, some coalescent
Surrounding infiltrated erythematous plaques and flatter patches with fine scale
Coexistence of patch, plaque and tumor lesions of different stages on the same limb
Focal superficial erosion/crusting over the largest nodule; no deep ulceration evident
describe_en: Clinical photograph of the lower extremity shows multiple violaceous to dusky red, dome-shaped tumor nodules, several coalescing into a larger indurated mass, arising on a background of infiltrated erythematous plaques and scaly patches. The simultaneous presence of patch, plaque and tumor lesions favors progression of a long-standing cutaneous T-cell lymphoma rather than a de novo nodular process. Histologic confirmation with assessment for large-cell transformation is required. Findings are consistent with tumor-stage mycosis fungoides.

ddx.dx: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma
ddx.vs: Typically presents as solitary or grouped ulcerating nodules without a preceding patch/plaque background, and shows sheets of CD30+ large cells.
Violaceous nodules occur without an evolving patch-plaque stage and biopsy shows MPO/CD33+ myeloid or monocytic infiltrate.

ddx.dx: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
ddx.vs: Rapidly growing red-violaceous leg tumors without prior patches; biopsy shows CD20+, BCL2+, MUM1+ large B cells.
Violaceous plaques and nodules are vascular spindle-cell lesions positive for HHV8 (LANA) rather than atypical CD4+ T cells.
